knowledgeAnswers.rationale: Trembling and attempts to leave are stress signs. The groomer stops, keeps a hand on the dog, lets it settle, and resumes only when calm.
An animal is never left unattended in a bath. The cat is removed first, or a second person holds it.
The lesson says an animal is never left tethered, fixed or unattended on a table or in a bath.

practicalCriteria: Assessor presents a simulated stressed animal and observes the candidate stop the task, keep a hand on the animal and resume only when calm
Assessor observes the candidate restrain a simulated dog at the lowest force that keeps it safe, with one hand on the animal on the raised surface
Assessor checks that the candidate never leaves a simulated animal tethered or unattended in the bath
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Job record for the simulated groom with the stress observation and action noted
Written statement of the welfare law position, with its source and date
stopWorkCriteria: An animal is left tethered, fixed or unattended on a table or in a bath
Force is used to finish a task after clear distress signs
A muzzle is fitted by a person not trained to fit it
